key_insight: Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials can screen crystal database entries for physical plausibility, but their validation results depend strongly on the model used.
engineering_relevance: MLIP-based relaxation offers a scalable first-pass quality check for large crystallography databases, helping prioritize structures for expert review.
method: Filtered 522,086 COD entries to 317,457 structurally usable crystals.
Relaxed the filtered set with M3GNet and checked convergence plus cell-volume change.
Compared M3GNet, CHGNet, PET-MAD, and PET-OAM on 524 manually selected structures to probe failure modes and error detection.
evidence_signal: In the filtered COD set, 314,153 of 317,457 entries converged with M3GNet, while a manual study of 327 structures showed that no single threshold on energy, force, or displacement cleanly separates valid from invalid cases.
watch_item: MLIP relaxations are model-dependent and can distort specific motifs, so a single potential should not be used as the sole validator.
paper_title: Assessing the Reliability of Foundational Machine Learning Potentials for Evaluating the Veracity of the Crystallography Open Database
